about: The film's house numbers, in one table that every calculator (kit/calculators) and tool reads, so the tools cannot drift apart. Read it with kit/calculators/settings.py (python3 settings.py show SECTION). Built from the inventory of 423 hand-found values (log 35, scratchpad plugin-calculators/inventory-and-design.json) and checked against the project's files. Sources name the austerity-explainer project's files: film-kit/... is the film kit, notes/... the project notes, "scratchpad redesign/..." the redesign rounds' working folder of log 34.
entry_format: Every number is {"value", "unit", "kind", "source"} (some add "note"). A section may hold groups of entries. Keys read with dots: frame.width_pixels. Builders add their own section (with an "about" line); they never change another section's numbers without saying so.

kinds.measured: the project measured it (a recording, a render, a bill, a fit to a picture): change it only by measuring again
kinds.judged: a person or a helper chose it by looking or by a rule of thumb: change it only after looking again
kinds.invented: nobody has tested it yet: a starting point; say so whenever a result rests on it

shot_kind_profiles.about: Which composing rules apply to each kind of shot, and their limits. still_life is the base (the notice corner, where the rules were measured); the other kinds list only what they change, taken from what the project kept. A view names one or more kinds (place facts "kind_of_shot"). settings.py resolve_profile() gives the rules a view is held to.
shot_kind_profiles.about_combining: For each rule, every named kind that changes it is used and the loosest wins: a rule switched off by any named kind is off; "max" limits take the largest, "min" limits the smallest, "range" the widest. A view's one-off exceptions go in its place facts "accepted" list, not here.

value: rule2: camera level and at eye height (it moves everything on screen)
rule1: the street's lines meet at the subject's edge (slide or move the subject, never turn)
rule12: words and story props clear of the phone buttons
rule7: some story thing reaches 0.70 down (wins over rule 8's bottom-left limit for the story things that make the reach)
people: figures at least 6 m away, backs turned, a crowd across the view (wins over rule 3's box width)
rule4: clear overlaps or clear gaps
rule8: work props small and far; nothing big at bottom left
rule5 and rule6: light, once the layout has settled
rule10: the quiet side's weight (the weakest: the checker ranks it 0.8)

interior.about: Indoors, props on counters, shelves and tables (3 of plan 34's 6 places: the checkout, the corner shop, the kitchen). Provisional: from checkout C1's checks 1-10 (16 October 2026), which nobody has accepted yet.

resting_on.unit: metres of air above a declared support surface (floor, counter, shelf, table)
resting_on.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-checkout/check1/report.md: four props on the 0.9 m counter falsely "landed on something high"; the check file needed on_ground [] (skeptic, log 35)
resting_on.note: "Landed high" (0.5 m above the street) does not apply indoors.

rule5_top_third_brightness.source: checkout-c1-shot-check.json "sky": "ceiling*" (the ceiling is the dim top)

rule7_story_reaches_down.source: checkout-c1-shot-check.json story_reaches_down (reach worked out above the counter top)
rule7_story_reaches_down.reach_above: the support surface the story stands on

dark_subject.about: A subject that is dark by nature (an iron gate, an open doorway): shown by lighting what is behind it, judged by its silhouette, not its brightness (W1's gate, W2's gateway).

rule1_meeting_point_gap.unit: share of the width, across only
rule1_meeting_point_gap.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): W2's gateway 0 px across but 117 px below the meeting point (0.108); W1 working: the meeting point lies inside the opened gateway
rule1_meeting_point_gap.measure: to the opening's whole outline; a meeting point inside the opening passes

rule5_subject_brightness_ratio.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): W1 gate 0.85 x the mean, W2 gateway 0.68, W1 working 0.64; round 5 raised the yard light 260 to 900 W and the gate still could not be brightest (inventory: a dark subject)

rule5_brightest_share_on_subject.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): W1 8%, W2 0%, W2 slowed 13%

rule5_brightest_share_in_story_box.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): W1 43%, W2 33%, W1 working 62%

rule5_nothing_in_story_as_bright.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): every story thing is brighter than a dark gate

rule6_lit_from_below.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): W1 0.06, W2 0.01, W2 slowed -0.10, W1 working -0.05 (a dark subject has no colour to warm)

rule10_nothing_on_quiet_side_outshines.source: scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md (round 5 final checks, 2026-10-16): a lit window or lamp always outshines a dark gate

silhouette_contrast.unit: (surround + 0.05)/(subject + 0.05) over a band round the subject
silhouette_contrast.source: People test: painted figures read at 2.20 on the film frame (film-figure-contrast.json)
silhouette_contrast.note: Measured on figures, not a gate: calibrate on the W1 painting.

shot_planner.about: The shot planner (calculators/plan_shot.py) and the shot checker's kinds of shot and accepted list (paper-film/tools/check_shot.py): margins, figure sizes and crowd tests. Added by the shot planner helper (log 35).

reach_aim_margin_down.unit: down the frame, past rule 7's reach
reach_aim_margin_down.source: The camera sums land within 0.006 to 0.015 of the rendered reach (core tests: W1 DIESEL drum 0.723 against the rendered 0.72; checkout C1 divider 0.776 against 0.78; man 6's feet 0.696 against his box bottom 0.704), so the planner aims 0.02 past the limit; round 5's W1 passed at 0.72 (scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-w1-quiet/report.md)

figure_shoes_below_feet_down.source: Core tests (log 35): a figure's feet point lands 0.0005 to 0.0111 above the bottom of its model's box from Blender (people test, 11 figures, people-test-shot.json film_frame_box) and 0.0076 for W1's man 6 (works-shot.json men_seen); a figure that misses the reach by less than this is a 'look'

right_edge_aim_margin_share.unit: share of the width, inside the must-read edge
right_edge_aim_margin_share.source: Design (log 35): the wanted meeting point is 0.895 - the subject's width - 0.01, so its right edge ends at 0.885 (check_shot.py's own fixes aim 0.005 inside the limit); untested

planning_spot_box.source: Design (log 35): keep the spots that can be worked out before rendering (meeting point, subject, story) inside 0.30 x 0.40, leaving room for the brightest parts and the warm light within the main rule's 0.40 x 0.50; rendered spans: notice corner 0.11 x 0.23 (log 31), checkout C1 0.22 x 0.10 (check 10)

figure_shoulder_width_metres.source: paper-film/blender/figures/build_figures.py: shoulder joints 0.175 m either side of the middle (SHOULDER_SIDE) and a coat chest ring 0.192 m half-wide, plus the sleeve (about 0.06 m, judged from the code); figures/index.json overall widths 0.53 to 0.66 m include the arms

figure_box_metres.source: figures/index.json size_metres of the five waiting men (widths 0.529 to 0.663 m, depths 0.47 to 0.833 m; medians 0.636 and 0.539): the box shot_facts.py measures round a figure, arms included

figure_head_width_metres.source: build_figures.py HEAD_HALF_SIZE (0.0775 m half width, without the cap)

face_visible_dot_min.unit: cosine between the figure's facing and the way to the camera
face_visible_dot_min.source: Inventory 'Head size decides painted or silhouette' (log 35): a face or profile shows when facing . to-camera > -0.2 (about 100 degrees); untested

sign_edge_on_degrees.unit: degrees between a sign's facing and the way to the camera
sign_edge_on_degrees.source: Plan 34 lines 85-87 ('a face seen at under about 20 degrees is edge-on and fails'); a drum's stencil uses its own wrap (lettering.stencil_wrap_degrees)

crowd_min_figures.source: Shot planner (log 35): a story group of 3 or more figures is judged as a crowd (its long axis, rows and heads)

crowd_axis_min_elongation.unit: spread along the long axis over the spread across it
crowd_axis_min_elongation.source: Shot planner (log 35): a group that spreads less than 1.5 times as far one way as the other has no long axis to line up along a view

slide_sample_steps.source: Design (log 35): cast the film frame's corners every 10% of the slide; people are judged from every step too

check_shot_silhouette_band_share_of_widt.source: check_shot.py's dark-subject test (log 35): the band round the subject's outline whose brightness is compared with the subject's (the people test measured its figure contrast over a band too, film-figure-contrast.json); untested on a gate

check_shot_accepted_worse_share.source: check_shot.py's accepted list (log 35): an accepted problem that has grown more than 5% past the number it was accepted at is a problem again

views_and_models.about: The house numbers of three tools: view_audit.py (lettering, figures and landmarks seen from each view), make_check_file.py (writes a view's shot check file from the Blender scene) and model_lint.py (model faults before plates). Added by the views-and-models helper (log 35).

lettering_material_patterns.unit: material name patterns (lower case, * any letters)
lettering_material_patterns.source: The naming the build scripts use: works-effects.js LETTERING (-lettering, -stencil, -printing), checkout-signs.glb (-lettering), notice-corner-signs.glb (notice-paper); inventory 'Lettering keeps its own surface; naming convention'

model_lint.about: model_lint.py: squashed textures (stripes), same-plane faces, floors over ground, names, glass, glows, sizes, fronts.

stripe_ratio_of_median.unit: share of the part's median texture area per square metre
stripe_ratio_of_median.source: scratchpad redesign/check-round-3/tools/find_stripes.py (its threshold found round 3's 15, 27 and 33 striped parts and round 4's 0; skeptic, log 35: not the design's 1e-3)

stripe_report_area_square_metres.unit: square metres of striped faces in one part
stripe_report_area_square_metres.source: find_stripes.py (round 3): parts with more striped area than this are listed

stripe_face_min_area_square_metres.source: find_stripes.py (round 3): smaller faces are left out of the median

same_plane_gap_metres.source: Inventory 'Two surfaces on the same plane flicker' (proposed: less than 0.1 mm apart); lesson 85's ceiling sat exactly on the slab. The fix's gap is models.coplanar_gap_metres (0.01)

same_plane_normal_cos.unit: cosine between the two faces' normals (facing the same way)
same_plane_normal_cos.source: Design (log 35): parallel normals; faces back to back (a prop's base on the ground) are left out because one hides the other

same_plane_overlap_min_square_metres.unit: square metres of overlap (or of raised floor) worth reporting
same_plane_overlap_min_square_metres.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): 10 cm by 1 cm; smaller slivers along shared edges are not worth a fix

upward_normal_z_min.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): a floor or ground face (the street's 4-degree slope is 0.998)

glass_material_patterns.source: Log 32 (the gas lamps' street_lamp_01_glass and the lantern's Lantern_01_glass took their see-through value from their pictures); set_dressing.see_through

glowing_base_brightness_max.source: Design (log 35) from lesson 89 (a glow lit by its own lamp renders white: glow materials get a black base, set_dressing.glow_material)

size_claim_tolerance_share.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): the jacket's 'about 0.6 m wide' against 0.516 measured (round 1) is 16% off

floor_min_square_metres.unit: square metres of a raised floor over another ground
floor_min_square_metres.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): a yard or a room's floor, not a window sill 5 cm over its opening (0.2 square metres each on the Works' cottages); round 2's yard setts covered about 2,000 square metres

view_audit.about: view_audit.py: letters in pixels at every view, drums' turns, loud unnamed signs, landmark tops in the words band, heads, signs' backs, continuity counts, title contrast.

must_read_facing_min_cos.unit: cosine between the sign's face and the way to the camera, across (the width of the letters)
must_read_facing_min_cos.source: Design (log 35) and inventory 'Words meant to be read face the camera' (flag under 0.85); no recorded case sets it

unnamed_sign_legibility_share_max.unit: letter pixels x letter brightness, as a share of the least legible named sign in the view
unnamed_sign_legibility_share_max.source: Calibrated on BANK in W3 (skeptic, log 35: about 0.5 of the boards'), against the least legible named sign that is itself readable: the No. 1 board, 14.7 px x 120 levels (the No. 2 board's 13.8 px is under lettering.not_meant_to_read_max_pixels). BANK lit, 29 px x 118 levels = 1.94 of it, was read first (round 3); dimmed to 0.3, 52 levels (measured) = 0.86, the critic still read it (round 4); the accepted dim 0.15 comes out 0.53 by dim_brightness_exponent (predicted, not measured). 0.55 separates them and asks for a dim of 0.157 (0.15 was chosen by eye)

dim_brightness_exponent.unit: levels = lit levels x dim ^ exponent
dim_brightness_exponent.source: Round 4 (round4-result.json): BANK's letters 118 levels lit, 52 at dim 0.3 (ln(52/118)/ln(0.3) = 0.68); the film's 57 against 128 gives 0.60. One sign, two points

figure_half_width_metres.unit: metres either side of a figure's feet
figure_half_width_metres.source: A working man's shoulders about 0.45-0.5 m (works-shot.json men_seen boxes: man 6 at 7.42 m spans 0.155 of the width = 0.58 m with his arms)

face_shows_within_degrees.unit: degrees between a figure's facing and the way to the camera
face_shows_within_degrees.source: Design (log 35); the people test showed faces are painted or not regardless (lesson 137; skeptic)

title_contrast_min.source: Inventory 'Title size and contrast' and 'Readable words: contrast and a dark band' (the common 4.5 to 1 for words; lessons 53, 66; log 32's faint amber 1926)

title_background_grow_pixels.source: Inventory 'Readable words: contrast and a dark band over busy sets' (the box widened 20 px)

check_file.about: make_check_file.py: what it generates (story roles come from the shot list).

on_ground_within_metres.unit: metres between a group's lowest point and a declared ground (road, pavement, ground, floor)
on_ground_within_metres.source: Design (log 35: within 0.05 m of the ground); check_shot.py's own resting limits are 0.03 floating and 0.05 sunk (composing.resting_*)

ground_kinds.unit: support surface kinds that count as the ground for check_shot's on_ground
ground_kinds.source: Skeptic (log 35): on_ground against declared support surfaces; check1 of the checkout (round 5) falsely reported four counter props 'landed on something high'

thin_pixels.unit: pixels across at the film frame (the group's narrow side)
thin_pixels.source: Design (log 35) and check_dark_picture.py (round 3-5 scratch wrapper: gate bars); composing.thin_parts_ignored_pixels_at_1080 is the same 6

dark_base_brightness.unit: area-weighted base colour brightness of a group's materials (linear, 0 to 1)
dark_base_brightness.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): near-black paint and iron (the notice board 0.016, the gates 0.015 measured here); the design's 0.08 was plate brightness, which does not exist before the plate is drawn

title_zone_fallback.unit: [left, top, right, bottom] shares of the frame
title_zone_fallback.source: Works check files title_zone; safe_area.title_band_down and text left/right (0.06, 0.90)

prop_collections.unit: collection name patterns where a place's assemble script puts props and figures
prop_collections.source: The kit's assemble scripts: assemble_notice_corner.py (props, signs), assemble_works.py (props, signs, gates, pop-up, men-no-1, men-no-2, workers-no-1, workers-no-2), assemble_checkout.py (checkout, signs); a shot list's prop_collections replaces it

light_prop_glow_share.unit: share of a story group's own surface that glows
light_prop_glow_share.source: Measured by make_check_file.py on the kept scenes (log 35): the hurricane lantern 0.23 (notice corner) and 0.21 (Works W1), both hand-made files' only light prop; the brazier with its coals 0.11 and 0.06, which the hand files and the skeptic keep out (log 31: its rim as bright as the notice was a real fault). Set between them

thin_fill_share.unit: share of a group's outline its faces fill, seen square on
thin_fill_share.source: views-and-models helper (log 35): iron gates and bars (the picture-match test misread them, rounds 3-5; check_dark_picture.py); a standing man fills about half his box

figure_collections.source: assemble_works.py (men-no-1, men-no-2, workers-no-1, workers-no-2); check_dark_picture.py left every waiting man out of the picture-match test (rounds 3-5)

page_timing.about: Page timing and words on screen: calculators/plan_page_timing.py, paper-film/tools/page_events.mjs and paper-film/tools/check_page_layout.mjs (log 35). The other numbers these tools read live in timing, safe_area, camera and checking. Added by the page timing helper.

settle_after_join_seconds.unit: seconds after a join ends, before the next page's first word
settle_after_join_seconds.source: Skeptic (log 35): the pause after a page = join.after + join.length + about 0.15 s to settle, plus any hold; clamped to 1.1-1.7 s only for plain peels

join_clear_of_next_word_seconds.source: Design (log 35), 'Page turn timing': each join must end at least 0.1 s before the next page's first word

pause_longer_than_needed_seconds.source: plan_page_timing.py: a pause this much longer than its join needs is reported as information (the extra is a rest before the next page)

conclusion_on_screen_seconds.unit: seconds from when it starts to appear until the cut (one frame short allowed)
conclusion_on_screen_seconds.source: Round 3 check (round3-result.json checked.findings[4]): '-> PRICES UP' on 'up' was up 0.65 s and could not be read; moved to 'prices' it was up 1.19 s before the cut and passed. That 1.2 s counts from appearing: at full strength it is 1.05 s (skeptic, log 35). timing.conclusion_full_strength_seconds names the same number but says full strength, which the accepted fix does not meet.

typed_word_window_seconds.unit: seconds either side of when the words show
typed_word_window_seconds.source: Inventory (log 35) 'Words on screen are short forms of what is said' (+-6 s). The design's +-3 s would fail round 4's accepted FLAT OUT = WORKING AS HARD AS THEY CAN, shown 4.7 s after 'working'.

overlap_opacity_min.unit: strength (0 to 1) both lines must have to count as overlapping
overlap_opacity_min.source: Design (log 35) overlay lint: two text boxes overlapping with both alpha above 0.1

overlap_pixels_min.unit: pixels two boxes must overlap by, across and down
overlap_pixels_min.source: plan_page_timing.py and check_page_layout.mjs: ignores boxes that only touch

number_hold_seconds.unit: seconds, plus seconds per character shown
number_hold_seconds.source: Log 19 (page 10's 5.6% never held still); inventory 'Numbers on screen held still and true to the ledger': 0.5 s + 0.15 s a character, about 1.5 s for 5.6%; at least timing.key_number_hold_seconds

count_end_after_word_max_seconds.unit: seconds after the number's spoken word
count_end_after_word_max_seconds.source: Lesson 53 and the plugin guide 'Hold the key number still': a count finishes on its word (design: count end <= the number word + 0.1 s)

still_after_event_seconds.unit: seconds after an event (or 0.05 s after its words are full, if later)
still_after_event_seconds.source: Design (log 35) 'Automatic still lists': every event + 0.25 s

page_turn_stills_after_last_word_seconds.unit: seconds after each page's last word
page_turn_stills_after_last_word_seconds.source: Workflows.md lines 120-121 (each last word + 0.7 s, drawn in one run of the chapter); design (log 35) adds 0.3 and 1.2 s

merge_stills_within_seconds.source: plan_page_timing.py: still times closer than this are drawn once

layout.about: check_page_layout.mjs: what it calls a pop, a hold and a moving camera.

pop_frames_max.unit: frames: a thing that comes or goes in this many frames or fewer, outside a planned cut, is a pop
pop_frames_max.source: Design (log 35) page pose sampler: any change completed in under 3 frames that is not a planned cut (log 27's one-frame faults: the scissors' jump, the padlock's glow switching on); lesson 86

pop_strength_change.unit: change in strength (0 to 1) that counts as coming or going

hold_without_still_key_frames.unit: frames of a held camera with no still key before it is reported
hold_without_still_key_frames.source: check_page_layout.mjs; a held shot without a still key draws the whole set every frame, about 5 times slower (design, log 35; filming.seconds_per_frame_* measured 0.9 s held against 4.3 s sliding)

camera_still_tolerance.unit: metres (and quaternion parts) a camera may differ between frames and still count as holding
camera_still_tolerance.source: check_page_layout.mjs (page_events.mjs rounds the camera to 0.0001 m)

jump_pixels_min.unit: pixels a drawn thing's middle may move in one frame before it counts as a jump
jump_pixels_min.source: check_page_layout.mjs; log 27's one-frame faults (the scissors' jump); old chapter 2's BARELY MOVE label flips 580 px between two frames
